college-1871.caption: Woodstock College in 1871, two years after it opened: the long front above the Patapsco, drawn by Arthur E. Jones, S.J., then a theologian in the house.
college-1871.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate facing the title of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 9. Public domain.

college-1920.caption: Woodstock, about 1920: the college from the garden side, in the year of its golden jubilee.
college-1920.credit: Woodstock Letters 49 (1920), no. 1, the Golden Jubilee number, plate before p. 1. Internet Archive woodstockletters4911unse, leaf 12. Public domain.

map-1877.caption: “Woodstock Cath. College” on the Patapsco, with Woodstock Station and Post Office on the Baltimore & Ohio, Granite, Marriottsville and the Howard County line across the river. Second District of Baltimore County, 1877, two inches to the mile.
map-1877.credit: G. M. Hopkins, Atlas of Baltimore County, Maryland (Philadelphia, 1877), plate 20 (detail). Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division, https://www.loc.gov/item/2018593339/. Public domain.

map-county-1877.caption: Where the journal was made: Woodstock Station in the south-western corner of Baltimore County, twenty miles from Baltimore by the B. & O., on the county map of 1877.
map-county-1877.credit: G. M. Hopkins, Atlas of Baltimore County, Maryland (Philadelphia, 1877), county map (detail). Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division, https://www.loc.gov/item/2018593339/. Public domain.

community-chart.caption: The community of Woodstock College, 1869–1919: faculty, theologians, philosophers and brothers, year by year, as the jubilee number drew them.
community-chart.credit: Woodstock Letters 49 (1920), no. 1, plate between pp. 12 and 13. Internet Archive woodstockletters4911unse, leaf 26. Public domain.

disputation.caption: The theological disputation in the library, at the golden jubilee of 1919.
disputation.credit: Woodstock Letters 49 (1920), no. 1, plate facing p. 23. Internet Archive woodstockletters4911unse, leaf 38. Public domain.

library.caption: The library, decorated for a celebration; the jubilee disputation of 1919 was held here.
library.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate between pp. 102 and 103 of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 125. Public domain.

mortuary-chapel.caption: The mortuary chapel in the cemetery above the college. The men buried around it fill the obituary section of the journal.
mortuary-chapel.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate between pp. 64 and 65 of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 83. Public domain.

funeral.caption: A Jesuit funeral at Woodstock: the procession from the college to the cemetery.
funeral.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate between pp. 64 and 65 of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 83. Public domain.

keller.caption: Joseph E. Keller, S.J. (1827–1886), provincial, rector of Woodstock and founder of the Woodstock Letters.
keller.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate facing p. 17 of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 29. Public domain.

mazzella.caption: Camillo Mazzella, S.J. (1833–1900), professor of dogma and first prefect of studies at Woodstock, later cardinal.
mazzella.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate facing p. 33 of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 47. Public domain.

pantanella.caption: Dominic Pantanella, S.J. (1831–1922), of the first faculty of 1869, the “creator of Woodstock's beauty”: its gardens, terraces and walks.
pantanella.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1, plate facing p. 49 of P. J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 65. Public domain.

pantanella-1920.caption: Dominic Pantanella, S.J., “sole survivor of the first faculty”, at the golden jubilee of 1919.
pantanella-1920.credit: Woodstock Letters 49 (1920), no. 1, plate facing p. 45. Internet Archive woodstockletters4911unse, leaf 65. Public domain.

dooley-title.caption: The title page of Patrick J. Dooley's Woodstock and Its Makers (The College Press, Woodstock 1927), the house history the journal printed in its 56th volume.
dooley-title.credit: Woodstock Letters 56 (1927), no. 1. Internet Archive woodstockletters5611unse, leaf 11. Public domain.
